title: Austin's Early Taxis, Police, and Building Boom
summary:
*   **Transportation:** Approved permits for "service cars," an early form of taxi service.
*   **Public Safety:** Appointed special policemen to serve as merchant police and private store watchmen.
*   **Urban Development:** Granted a permit for the construction of a new warehouse and storage tank.
*   **Citizen Concerns:** Heard from an attorney representing a citizen regarding a property dispute.

REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL:
Austin, Texas, November 10, 1921,
The Council was called to order by the Mayor. Roll call showed the following members
present: Mayor Yett, Councilmen Copeland, Eyres, Haynes and Searight, 5; absent, none.
The Minutes of the last meeting were read, and upon motion of Councilman Copeland, were
adopted by the following vote: Ayes, Kayor Yett, Councilmen Copeland, Eyres, Haynes and
Searight, 5; nayes, none.
Upon the recommendation of Sam D. Griffin, Chief of Police, Councilman Copeland nominated
J. Bunyon Prestidge as special policeman to act as merchant police. Nomination was
confirmed by the following vote: Ayes, Mayor Yett, Councilmen Eyres, Haynes and Searight,
4; nayes, none, Councilman Copeland not voting.
Upon the recommendation of Sam D. Griffin, Chief of Police, Councilman Copeland nominated
J. Rector Allen as special policeman to act as watchman at E, M. Scarbrough & Son's Store.
Homination was confirmed by the following vote: Ayes, Mayor Yett, Councilmen Eyres, Haynes
and Searight, 4; nayes, none, Councilman Copeland not voting.

Searight.
The Minutes of the last meeting were read and upon motion of Councilman Haynes were

The IIth Annual Report of the United Charities Association was read by the Secretary, Miss

Councilman Searight appeared at 10:30 A. M.
